This water would by no means be fit for drinking, but would be suitable for industrial purposes. In turn, Montana Resources will draw water from another toxic sink they have on site, known as the Yankee Doodle Tailings Pond; bring it through not just one, but a series of treatment plants that thoroughly remove toxic metals and chemicals; then discharge it into local waterways. Taking old toxic water out of Yankee Doodle will create space for new toxic water from the Pit to be pumped in.

This water shuffle must be done carefully, because if too much water is drawn from the Pit, the tunnels that underlie the city of Butte will lose pressure and collapse, and vast sections of the city could sink into toxic hell. Although it isn’t the subject of discussion for much of the mainstream public, this seemingly absurd cleanup timespan that stretches to infinity is normal for big mining operations. For international travel I like to fly in somewhere with a hiking backpack and a couple changes of clothes and then just wander around for one or two months. People I meet will recommend places they've been and I'll go to those places if they seem cool. I'll stay at hostels, with people I meet, sometimes on the street. Eat out of markets, not restaurants. Usually manage all costs at $10 a day.

I have friends who do this in a more extreme way, they stay long past running out of money and start working (illegally) wherever they are, taking up whatever odd jobs, agricultural seasonal work, construction, street performer, exotic dancing, whatever, to get enough money for the next leg of the trip, then they move on. One of my friends traveled for a bit over ten years with no money to start with and no money at the end.

Traveling in the US when I need to go out of state, I'll drive, and make a long trip of it with many detours. Generally sleep in the car at rest stops and at camp grounds with a small tent. And occasionally drop in on friends or distant relatives if passing through their area.

I've never made concrete detailed plans on any trip. Often there's some concrete part of it, like get to some state for a music festival or to meet with a client on a certain date, but the rest is improvised.
Not on a plane, but have in a car. Usually have a vague idea of what we'd like to do, but find out that the unplanned stops are the most enjoyable.
